workflow.name: Refactor with a checkpoint
workflow.description: Plans the refactor, waits for a person to approve the plan, then carries it out. Good for anything touching code you cannot afford to break.

skills.name: plan-the-refactor
skills.description: Plans a behaviour-preserving refactor for a person to approve.
skills.skill_md_content:
---
name: plan-the-refactor
description: Plans a behaviour-preserving refactor for a person to approve.
---

Plan this refactor. Do not change any code yet.

Goal: ${task_title}

${task_body}

Refactors go wrong when they quietly change behaviour, so be specific: which
files move, what stays identical, and what could break. List anything you are
unsure about. A person is going to read this and decide whether to let it run.

Write the plan into an output block named `plan`.

skills.name: carry-out-the-refactor
skills.description: Executes an approved refactor without changing behaviour.
skills.skill_md_content:
---
name: carry-out-the-refactor
description: Executes an approved refactor without changing behaviour.
---

Carry out this approved refactor:

${plan}

Behaviour must not change. Run the tests before you start so you know what
already passes, and again at the end. If something has to change behaviour to
work, stop and say so instead of doing it.
